title: Perception: Direct/Ecological Theory (Gibson), Processing Theory (Gregory)
summary: Direct or ecological theory of perception (J. J. Gibson); processing theory of perception (Richard Gregory); template matching; prototype theory; geon theory; pandemonium model.
objectives: Explain template matching, prototype theory, geon theory, and pandemonium model.
revision: Gibson = direct/ecological (environment provides affordances). Gregory = top-down constructive (hypothesis testing). Template matching, prototype theory, geon theory, pandemonium model are constructive models.
traps: Gibson = direct, environment provides all information.
Gregory = top-down, hypotheses from prior knowledge.
confusions: Believing template matching allows for variation.

notes.t: Gibson proposed that perception is direct — the environment provides sufficient information (affordances, optic flow, invariants) for perception without internal constructive processing.
Gregory proposed top-down processing: perception is a hypothesis-testing process where prior knowledge and expectations shape interpretation of sensory input.
Perception occurs by comparing incoming sensory input with stored templates. Exact match leads to recognition.
Recognition occurs by comparing input with the best example (prototype) of a category rather than exact templates.
Biederman's geon theory proposes that objects are recognized from basic geometric shapes (geons) such as cylinders, cubes, and cones.
Selfridge's pandemonium model proposes parallel processing through feature demons, cognitive demons, and a decision demon that shouts loudest.
UGC NET frequently asks to contrast Gibson (direct/ecological) with Gregory (top-down/constructive) theories of perception.
